# Lighting

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("Lighting")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Controls the time of day, the sun and the ambient light of the world. The sun is not an instance: its direction is computed from `ClockTime` and `GeographicLatitude`.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Ambient` | `Color3` | — | read/write | The uniform light on surfaces in enclosed spaces, such as a cave, a tunnel or the underside of an overhang, which see none of the sky. A surface that sees part of the sky is lit by a blend of this and `OutdoorAmbient`. It stands in for bounced light, so a cave is dim instead of black; lower it for a darker cave. It is not clamped and can exceed 1. |
| `AutoExposure` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the brightness of the picture adapts to what the camera sees, as an eye does when it moves from a cave into daylight. When it is off, the exposure is fixed, so a darker world looks darker. `ExposureCompensation` applies in both cases. A machine whose graphics settings turn automatic exposure off ignores this property. |
| `Brightness` | `number` | — | read/write | The strength of the sun, independent of its color. |
| `ClockTime` | `number` | — | read/write | The time of day, in hours from 0 to 24. A value outside the range wraps around, so a script can add to it every tick. Together with `GeographicLatitude`, it sets the direction of the sun. |
| `EnvironmentDiffuseScale` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much the sky lights matte surfaces, from 0 to 1. At 0 a surface is lit only by the sun, by lights and by `Ambient`. The sky itself is drawn the same at any value. |
| `EnvironmentSpecularScale` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much shiny surfaces reflect the sky, from 0 to 1. At 0 metal reflects only the sun's highlight, which suits an interior that the sky does not reach. |
| `ExposureCompensation` | `number` | — | read/write | An adjustment to the exposure, in EV stops, added to the automatic exposure. At 0 the automatic exposure is used as measured; +1 doubles the light and -1 halves it. It is not clamped. |
| `ExposureMax` | `number` | `1.5849625` | read/write | The most the automatic exposure can brighten the picture, in EV stops, as the world gets darker. The default is about 1.5, so a night is darker than a day but still visible.<br><br>Lower it for a darker night. At 0 the exposure never brightens, and a world lit a third as brightly looks a third as bright. Set `ExposureMin` and `ExposureMax` to the same value to fix the exposure there. |
| `ExposureMin` | `number` | `-2.7369655` | read/write | The most the automatic exposure can darken the picture, in EV stops, as the world gets brighter. The default is about -2.75. Raise it toward 0 to keep bright places bright, so that snow glares and a desert at noon is hard to look at. |
| `FogColor` | `Color3` | — | read/write | The color that distant objects fade toward between `FogStart` and `FogEnd`. It is kept but not used while an `Atmosphere` is directly under `Lighting`. |
| `FogEnd` | `number` | — | read/write | The distance at which fog hides everything, in meters. A value equal to or below `FogStart` turns fog off. |
| `FogStart` | `number` | — | read/write | The distance at which fog begins, in meters. It is kept but not used while an `Atmosphere` is directly under `Lighting`. |
| `GeographicLatitude` | `number` | — | read/write | The latitude of the world, in degrees north of the equator. It tilts the path of the sun across the sky. |
| `GlobalShadows` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the sun, or the moon at night, casts shadows. Turn it off for the look of an overcast day or for a stylized world without shadows. Lights that cast shadows still do. |
| `OutdoorAmbient` | `Color3` | — | read/write | The uniform light on surfaces that see the open sky. It is equal to `Ambient` by default, so a world that sets neither is lit the same indoors and outdoors. For dark caves, lower `Ambient` alone. A part is outdoors unless terrain covers it. |
| `ShadowSoftness` | `number` | `0.2` | read/write | How soft the edges of the sun's shadows are, from 0 (as sharp as the shadow map allows) to 1 (a penumbra of a quarter of a meter on each side of the edge). |
| `SunDirection` | `vector` | — | read-only | The unit vector that points from the world toward the sun. It is computed only from `ClockTime` and `GeographicLatitude`, so the same values always give the same direction. |
